assumptions: The customer-facing impact is taken from the service's error-rate metrics over 18:25-18:31; the number of distinct shoppers affected was not measured.

The defect at monthly_statement.py:627 is inferred from the error logs and from the fact that reverting the flag restored baseline; the specific input condition that produces the empty iterable has not been reproduced or root-caused in code.
One production change event was retrieved for the 150 minutes before the alert but was not implicated; the flag toggle, not a deploy, lines up with the 18:25 onset.
The 18:25 log line shows a mixed evaluation (97 off / 103 on), suggesting the flag was ramped rather than flipped for all traffic at once; the exact rollout configuration was not confirmed.
Recovery is judged from the error rate returning to baseline after the revert, not from an independent check that account pages render correctly for the previously failing accounts.
The ClientDisconnected errors seen before 18:25 are treated as ordinary background noise within the pre-incident baseline, not as a precursor.
input.executive_summary:
On 26 September 2026, some customers trying to open their account page got an error instead. The problem started at 18:25 UTC and the page was working normally again by 18:31 UTC — about six minutes in total. During that window a large minority of account-page views failed, according to the service's own measurements; the rest of the shop was unaffected, and nothing customers had already done was lost or corrupted.

The cause was a newly switched-on feature for showing monthly spending. It worked for most shoppers but crashed for accounts whose data it did not expect. The automated incident responder (Argus) picked up the alert, traced the failures to that feature, switched it back off, and verified that errors returned to their normal level before closing the response. A draft code fix has been opened for review so the feature can be turned on again safely.

Note on timings: the roughly six-minute figure is how long customers were affected. Argus's own handling time, from alert to confirmed mitigation, was under a minute and should not be read as the outage length.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was switched from off to on at 18:25, which enabled a code path in `src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:627` that calls `max()` on a collection that is empty for some accounts, raising `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty` and failing that share of account-page requests. Turning the flag back off restored the service to baseline, confirming the flag-gated path as the cause.
